newsitem.title: TURKEY: Erbakan says Turkey security scandal being probed.
newsitem.headline: Erbakan says Turkey security scandal being probed.

text.p: Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said Turkey is using all its resources to investigate a scandal over alleged links between organised crime and the security apparatus that has rocked the government.

"The state is not at all deaf to the allegations that have come out because of this. All the state's resources are being used to carry out the necessary procedures," Anatolian news agency quoted Erbakan as saying on Sunday night.
Erbakan said the interior ministry, the national intelligence service and his office were looking into a fatal crash this month that sparked the scandal.
A senior policeman, beauty queen and fugitive gangster died in the same car in an accident near the western town of Susurluk.
Government MP Sedat Bucak, who heads an anti-guerrilla Kurdish militia, was also in the vehicle. Seven guns and two silencers were found in the wreckage.
Erbakan said he had discussed the scandal, which forced the interior minister to resign two weeks ago, with President Suleyman Demirel on Sunday.
